entry.title: Portixeddu Beach, Buggerru
entry.summary: Portixeddu is a long beach of golden sand on the Costa Verde of south-west Sardinia, backed by tall dunes and a river mouth. Waves and winds from the west make it popular with surfers. A mining town and the great dune of Piscinas lie nearby.

entry.title: Li Mindi Beach, Badesi
entry.summary: Li Mindi is a wide beach of golden sand in Badesi on the north coast of Sardinia, backed by dunes and Mediterranean scrub near the mouth of the Coghinas river. The sea is shallow and clear, and the beach is quieter than the better-known resorts of the Costa Paradiso.

entry.title: Cala Mari Pintau, Sardinia
entry.summary: Cala Mari Pintau is a small cove of white sand and rocks on the south-east coast of Sardinia, with very clear water and low granite cliffs on either side. An old watchtower stands on the headland above the cove, and the coast road leads to the neighbouring beaches.

entry.title: Solanas Beach, Sardinia
entry.summary: Solanas is a long beach of fine pale sand on the south-east coast of Sardinia, with low dunes, juniper bushes and a sea that is calm and clear. The beach lies on the road between Cagliari and Villasimius and is quieter than the main town beaches.

entry.title: Isola Rossa Beach, Sardinia
entry.summary: Isola Rossa is a small seaside village on the north coast of Sardinia, named after a red porphyry island joined to the shore, with a Genoese tower on top. A beach of coarse sand lies beside the harbour, and the water is clear. Granite rocks and Mediterranean scrub frame the village.

entry.title: Santa Maria Navarrese Beach, Ogliastra
entry.summary: Santa Maria Navarrese is a small resort on the east coast of Sardinia, with a bay of sand and pebbles beside a Spanish watchtower and an ancient olive tree near the church. Boats leave from the harbour for the famous coves of the Gulf of Orosei, and the red mountains of Ogliastra rise behind the village.

entry.title: Le Bombarde Beach, Alghero
entry.summary: Le Bombarde is a bay of fine white sand north of Alghero on the north-west coast of Sardinia, with clear turquoise water and pine trees behind the shore. The water is shallow and sheltered, and the cape of Capo Caccia can be seen in the distance.

entry.title: Marina del Cantone Beach, Nerano
entry.summary: Marina del Cantone is a small fishing hamlet at the end of the Sorrento peninsula, with a beach of pebbles and a few boats on the shore. The water is very clear, and the island of Capri can be seen across the strait. Family restaurants along the shore are known for fresh fish and for pasta with courgettes.

entry.title: Trentova Beach, Agropoli
entry.summary: Trentova is a long beach of sand and fine pebbles south of Agropoli on the Cilento coast of Campania, with a gentle slope into the sea. The old town of Agropoli with its castle stands on a headland a short drive away, and the Greek temples of Paestum lie to the north.

entry.title: Acciaroli Beach, Cilento
entry.summary: Acciaroli is a quiet fishing village on the Cilento coast of Campania, with a harbour, a small beach of sand and fine pebbles and clear water. The village has narrow streets, a medieval tower and a relaxed feel. The Cilento National Park lies behind the coast.

entry.title: Praia a Mare Beach, Calabria
entry.summary: Praia a Mare is a seaside town on the Tyrrhenian coast of Calabria, with a long beach of sand and small pebbles that faces the island of Dino. The water is clear and warm in summer, and sea caves lie along the coast nearby. A seafront promenade runs behind the beach.

entry.title: Vignanotica Beach, Gargano
entry.summary: Vignanotica is a cove of white pebbles at the foot of tall white limestone cliffs on the Gargano coast, south of Vieste. A natural rock arch stands at one end, and the water is a deep turquoise. The beach is reached by a steep path from a car park or by boat.

entry.title: Playa de Santa Ponsa, Mallorca
entry.summary: Santa Ponsa is a sheltered bay on the south-west coast of Mallorca with a wide beach of fine sand and calm, shallow water. Pine-covered headlands close the bay on both sides. A promenade runs along the shore with cafes and small shops, and the bay is popular with families.

entry.title: Praia da Batata, Lagos
entry.summary: Praia da Batata is the main town beach of Lagos in the Algarve, a wide strip of golden sand beside the old fort and the harbour. A short tunnel in the cliffs leads from the old town to the sand. The beach is busy in summer but easy to reach on foot.

entry.title: Praia da Prainha, Alvor
entry.summary: Praia da Prainha is a small cove of golden sand between limestone cliffs near Alvor in the Algarve. The beach is sheltered from the wind, and the water is clear. Stairs lead from the clifftop to the sand, and the cove fills early in summer.

entry.title: Praia Verde, Castro Marim
entry.summary: Praia Verde is a quiet beach on the eastern Algarve, with fine sand and a pine forest behind the shore, between Monte Gordo and Manta Rota. The sea is warmer than on the west coast, and the beach has a relaxed feel. A walking path through the pines links it to Monte Gordo.

entry.title: Praia da Consolacao, Peniche
entry.summary: Praia da Consolacao is a long beach of fine sand on the coast near Peniche, popular with surfers and with families. The water is Atlantic and cool, and the beach is wide at low tide. Fields, small dunes and a few restaurants lie behind the sand.

entry.title: Praia da Lagoa de Albufeira, Sesimbra
entry.summary: Praia da Lagoa de Albufeira is a wide beach on the Atlantic coast south of Lisbon, beside a lagoon that opens to the sea in winter. Dunes and low cliffs surround the shore, and the waves attract surfers and kitesurfers. The lagoon is calm for children when it is open.

entry.title: Praia da Fonte da Telha, Costa da Caparica
entry.summary: Praia da Fonte da Telha is a long and wide beach of golden sand at the southern end of the Costa da Caparica, backed by sandy cliffs and a protected landscape. It is quieter than the beaches near Lisbon, and the waves are good for surf. A few beach restaurants stand behind the sand.

entry.title: Praia de Sao Pedro do Estoril
entry.summary: Praia de Sao Pedro do Estoril is a small beach of sand and rocks on the coast between Lisbon and Cascais, beside the seaside railway. The water is Atlantic and cool, and a promenade links the beach with the neighbouring towns. It is popular with locals on summer weekends.

entry.title: Praia de Santa Rita, Torres Vedras
entry.summary: Praia de Santa Rita is a wide beach of golden sand on the Silver Coast, below low cliffs and fields near Torres Vedras. The waves are Atlantic and strong, and the beach is quiet outside the summer months. A path from the village leads down to the shore.

entry.title: Agios Nikitas Beach, Lefkada
entry.summary: Agios Nikitas is a small village on the north-west coast of Lefkada, with a beach of pebbles and clear turquoise water. The village has no traffic in the centre, and a path leads to a second pebble beach called Milos. Steep hills with olive trees and pines surround the bay.

entry.title: Vasiliki Beach, Lefkada
entry.summary: Vasiliki is a village at the head of a long bay on the south of Lefkada, famous as one of the best windsurfing spots in Greece. The beach is made of fine pebbles, and the wind rises in the afternoon. Boats leave the harbour for the beaches of the west coast and for the islands.

entry.title: Nikiana Beach, Lefkada
entry.summary: Nikiana is a small seaside village on the east coast of Lefkada, with a long beach of pebbles, calm water and a view of the mainland hills. The beach is quieter than the famous beaches on the west coast. Tavernas stand along the promenade, and the water is warm in summer.

entry.title: Damouchari Beach, Pelion
entry.summary: Damouchari is a small bay on the Pelion peninsula, with a beach of pebbles, a few old stone houses and a tiny harbour. Dense green hills drop to the water, and the sea is clear and calm. The bay was used as a film location, and only a few tavernas stand at the shore.

entry.title: Plage de Valras, Herault
entry.summary: Valras-Plage is a seaside resort on the Herault coast, close to Beziers, with a long beach of fine sand and shallow water. A promenade and cafes line the shore, and the Orb river runs into the sea at one end. The beach is popular with families and is lively in summer.

entry.title: Plage du Barcares, Pyrenees-Orientales
entry.summary: Le Barcares is a seaside resort near Perpignan with a very long, wide beach of fine sand and a gentle slope into the sea. A lagoon lies behind the town, and the Pyrenees can be seen on clear days. The beach is popular with families and sailing clubs.

entry.title: Plage de La Ciotat, Provence
entry.summary: La Ciotat is a Mediterranean harbour town between Marseille and Toulon, with a long beach of sand and a gentle slope into the sea. The beach is known as one of the few sandy beaches in the area, and the old port and the cliffs of the Bec de l Aigle are close by. Rocky coves lie along the coast on either side.

entry.title: Plage d Arcachon, Gironde
entry.summary: Arcachon is a seaside town on the bay of the same name in south-west France, with a long promenade and a sandy beach along the shore. The water inside the bay is calm, shallow and sheltered from the Atlantic waves. Oyster huts and the Dune du Pilat lie a short distance away.

entry.title: Plage des Minimes, La Rochelle
entry.summary: The Plage des Minimes is a sandy beach beside the large marina of La Rochelle on the Atlantic coast. The tide goes out far and leaves a wide strip of sand. The beach is a short bike ride from the old harbour, and boats from the marina fill the view.
